title: Proving constructive dismissal in an Indian employment context
p1:
Can an employee be forced to resign without anyone saying the words “you are fired”?

Sometimes, the answer may be yes — and that is where constructive dismissal enters the picture.
p2:
Many people believe dismissal only happens when a company issues a termination letter. But in some situations, drastic changes in work conditions can make an employee’s position practically impossible to continue.

A sudden unfair transfer, major reduction in responsibilities, exclusion from work, or a serious breach of employment terms may become relevant factors.
p3:
Proving constructive dismissal is not just about showing that a workplace became uncomfortable. The employee usually needs to demonstrate that the employer’s actions were serious enough to leave no reasonable choice except resignation.

The key lesson: a resignation on paper does not always tell the full story behind why an employee left.
conclusion: Do you think a resignation should always be treated as voluntary, or can workplace pressure sometimes amount to forced exit?
